'''Taue Odori''' (田植踊) is a form of {{ill|Yoshuku|ja|予祝芸能|lt=Yoshuku performing arts}} and {{ill|Ta-asobi|ja|田遊び|lt=tanuki-themed ceremonies}}, primarily performed in the {{ill|Tōhoku region|af|Tohoku|ar|منطقة توهوكو|az|Tohoku regionu|azb|توهوکو بؤلگه‌سی|ban|Wawengkon Tōhoku|bcl|Rehiyon Tōhoku|be|Тахоку|bg|Тохоку|bn|তোওহোকু অঞ্চল|ca|Regió de Tōhoku|ckb|ناوچەی تۆھۆکو|cs|Tóhoku|cy|Tōhoku|da|Tōhoku|de|Tōhoku|eo|Tōhoku|es|Región de Tōhoku|et|Tōhoku|eu|Tōhoku eskualdea|fa|منطقه توهوکو|fi|Tōhoku|fr|Région du Tōhoku|frr|Tōhoku|ga|Tōhoku|gl|Rexión de Tōhoku|hak|Tōhoku|he|טוהוקו|hi|तोहोकू क्षेत्र|hr|Tōhoku|hu|Tóhoku|hy|Տոհոկու (տարածաշրջան)|id|Wilayah Tōhoku|ilo|Rehion ti Tōhoku|is|Tōhoku|it|Tōhoku|ja|東北地方|ka|ტოჰოკუ|km|តំបន់ថូហុគឹ|ko|도호쿠 지방|la|Tōhoku|lt|Tohoku regionas|lv|Tohoku reģions|mk|Тохоку|mr|तोहोकू|ms|Kawasan Tōhoku|my|တိုးဟိုခု ဒေသ|nl|Tōhoku (regio)|nn|Tohokuregionen|no|Tōhokuregionen|oc|Tōhoku|pam|Tōhoku labuad|pl|Region Tōhoku|pnb|ٹوہوکو|pt|Tohoku (região)|qu|Tōhoku suyu|ro|Regiunea Tōhoku|ru|Тохоку|sc|Tōhoku|sco|Tōhoku region|sd|ٽوهوڪو ريجن|sh|Tōhoku|si|තෝහොකු කලාපය|simple|Tōhoku region|sk|Tóhoku|sl|Tohoku|sr|Тохоку|su|Wewengkon Tōhoku|sv|Tohoku|th|โทโฮกุ|tl|Tōhoku|tr|Tōhoku|uk|Регіон Тохоку|ur|توہوکو علاقہ|uz|Tōhoku viloyati|vi|Tōhoku|war|Tōhoku (rehiyon)|wuu|东北地方|zh|东北地方|zh_min_nan|Tôhoku tē-hng|zh_yue|東北地方|qid=Q129465|lt=Tohoku region}} of Japan, particularly in {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|en|Miyagi Prefecture|qid=Q47896|lt=Miyagi Prefecture}} and {{ill|Iwate Prefecture|en|Iwate Prefecture|qid=Q48326|lt=Iwate Prefecture}}, during the {{ill|First Full Moon Festival|en|First Full Moon Festival|qid=Q13423452|lt=Small New Year}} season. It is believed to have evolved into a {{ill|Furyū-odori|ja|風流踊}}.

== Overview ==

Unlike {{ill|Ta-asobi|ja|田遊び|lt=tanuki-themed ceremonies}}, which often simulate {{ill|Rice Cultivation|ja|稲作|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/rice cultivation|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q734080}} through symbolic gestures, Taue Odori is characterized by its strong {{ill|performing arts in Japan|ja|芸能|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/performance art|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11615913}} aspects. It is typically performed by {{ill|Village (Japan)|ja|村|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q4174776}} {{ill|Youth|en|Youth|qid=Q190007|lt=youth}}, {{ill|Boy|en|Boy|qid=Q3010|lt=boys}}, and {{ill|Girl|en|Girl|qid=Q3031|lt=girls}}, accompanied by a leader called "Yajuro" and wearing {{ill|Hanagasa|ja|花笠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/decorative flower hats|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11615624}}. Performers visit {{ill|Dwelling|en|Dwelling|qid=Q699405|lt=households}}, performing songs and dances, often following a recitation by Yajuro.

In some cases, the performance begins with a {{ill|Votive offering|en|Votive offering|qid=Q2601788|lt=dedication}} at {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=shrines}} or {{ill|Buddhist temple|en|Buddhist temple|qid=Q5393308|lt=temples}} before visiting homes. Variations exist, such as the inclusion of {{ill|Ta-no-Kami|en|Ta-no-Kami|qid=Q7683716|lt=rice-field gods}} and {{ill|Seven Lucky Gods|en|Seven Lucky Gods|qid=Q846858|lt=Seven Lucky Gods}}, celebrating the {{ill|New Year|en|New Year|qid=Q34812|lt=New Year}} in unique ways.
